subject: Request: SDLC evidence for code review sampling & CI segregation - AtlasBank

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@assessorco.com>

Cc: security@atlasbank.com
Date: Thu, 03 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AtlasBank SDLC intake — sampling & CI segregation questions

Hi Grace / Marissa,

We're kicking off the SDLC evidence intake for AtlasBank's SIG review. To keep the assessor pass window tight, can you provide the following by EOD next Monday (2025-04-07):

1) A code-review sampling matrix showing PR IDs, approvers, and a short rationale for why each PR was selected (sampling should cover high-risk repos + recent hotfixes).
2) A short diagram and narrative that explains CI runner segregation and network zoning for third-party runners (we need to validate that build agents for customer-facing services are isolated from infra pipelines).
3) Evidence that secrets used in CI are ephemeral and rotated (rotation cadence and example rotation event audit).
4) An attestation that commits to production branches are signed and how signing keys are protected / rotated.

If you can also drop a short mapping table (which artifact maps to each SIG question) that's perfect. If any of the asks require additional time, let us know which ones and we can scope a follow-up.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Security Assessor — AssessorCo

Grace / team,

Uploading the CI artifacts now — attached are the following stubs:
- ci-agent-network-diagram.png (PNG, 1.2MB) — diagram showing runner pools, VPCs, and control-plane access.
- sdlc-sampling-matrix.csv (CSV) — initial 12 PR rows covering three repos flagged by AtlasBank: gateway, auth-service, docs-site.

Notes (short answers inline):
1) CI runner segregation: build agents for customer-facing services run in dedicated VPC subnets (runner-pool-customer) with egress rules to our artifact registry only. Infra pipelines (terraform, infra-ops) run in a separate VPC (runner-pool-infra) with restricted IAM roles. We also enforce node isolation via runtime profiles and host-level mTLS. Diagram attached.

2) Ephemeral secrets: all CI secrets are provisioned via Vault dynamic secrets for short-lived tokens (default TTL = 1h, renewable to 8h with approval). For long-lived credentials (e.g., deploy keys) we store wrapped versions in KMS and require an approval plugin to unwrap during the release job.

Evidence provided:
- sample rotation event (logs) uploaded to Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/AtlasBank/SDLC_evidence/pack_v1/rotation_event_20250329.log
- Vault lease audit snippet included as an excerpt in the Drive folder.

3) Mapping: I started a simple mapping doc in the Drive folder called mapping_notes.md.

If Samir needs redacted logs or a deeper runbook excerpt, I can prepare by EOD Mon.

Attachments: [ci-agent-network-diagram.png (image/png)], [sdlc-sampling-matrix.csv (text/csv)]

Irene

Samir — attaching our packaged response for AtlasBank's intake. Please find:

- sdlc-sampling-matrix.csv (12 PRs with links and selection rationale)
- ci-agent-network-diagram.png (high-level runner segregation diagram)
- commit-signing-keys-attestation.pdf (attestation describing key custody, HSM usage, rotation cadence)

Quick summary:
- Code review: PR sample covers recent production hotfixes + high-risk services. All PRs shown have at least one independent approver and automated LGTM gating (see CSV column "gates").
- CI segregation: customer-facing builds run in an isolated runner pool with egress limited to our artifact registry; infra builds are separate and have restricted IAM. Diagram and short narrative attached.
- Secrets management: Vault dynamic secrets by default (TTL=1h), KMS-wrapped for long-lived keys, rotation audit snippet included in Drive.
- Commit signing: enforced for protected branches; private signing keys are stored in an HSM-backed KMS (rotation annually, emergency rotation playbook in Drive).

Attachments are in the Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.com/AtlasBank/SDLC_evidence/pack_v1 — if you need a redacted rotation audit or a PKI export for the signed commit sample, say the scope and we'll produce.

Question for the assessor: for the code-review sampling, do you want a larger sample (we can expand to 25 PRs) or is the current 12 sufficient for AtlasBank's acceptance criteria?

Thanks — open to a quick 20-min call if easier.

Best,
